title: Who Pays for the Knowledge Models Copy? Model Collapse as Rogers' Paradox
abstract: arXiv:2611.06022v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Generative models trained on the output of earlier models lose knowledge across generations, rare knowledge first. The remedies that work all bring in information from outside the loop, and the theory of model collapse treats that supply as given: a fixed archive, drawn from a fixed distribution. We argue that the supply is the problem, and that cultural evolution has the theory of it. We read model collapse as Rogers' paradox: a population that comes to rely on copying ends up no better off than one that never copied, because copies go stale unless someone keeps learning for themselves. We test the identification in three steps. First, Rogers' model, fitted only to fully synthetic training, predicts to within a few percentage points how much rare knowledge language models, from word trigrams to a pretrained transformer, retain under other mixtures of fresh data. Second, when the world itself changes, a lineage that copies its own past

translated_title: 谁为模型复制的知识买单？作为罗杰斯悖论的模型坍塌
translated_abstract: 在先前模型输出上训练的生成模型会在代际间丢失知识，且稀有知识最先丢失。行之有效的补救措施都需要从循环外部引入信息，而现有的模型坍塌理论将这些信息供给视为既定条件：一个来自固定分布的固定档案库。我们认为供给本身才是问题的根源，而文化演化早已拥有关于这一问题的理论。我们将模型坍塌解读为罗杰斯悖论：一个逐渐依赖复制的人口最终并不比从不复制的人口境况更好，因为复制品会过时，除非有人持续进行自主学习。我们通过三个步骤检验这一论证。第一，仅用完全合成训练数据拟合的罗杰斯模型，能够以几个百分点以内的误差，预测语言模型——从词三元组模型到预训练Transformer——在其他新鲜数据混合比例下保留多少稀有知识。第二，当世界本身发生变化时，复制自身过往的谱系……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文将模型坍塌重新解读为文化演化中的罗杰斯悖论，指出问题的根源在于外部信息供给本身，并证明仅用完全合成数据拟合的罗杰斯模型能精确预测语言模型在不同新鲜数据混合比例下稀有知识的保留量。
en_tdlr: This paper reframes model collapse as Rogers' paradox from cultural evolution, arguing that the problem lies in the information supply itself, and demonstrates that Rogers' model fitted solely to fully synthetic training accurately predicts how much rare knowledge language models retain under various mixtures of fresh data.
